axes.brief:
Competitive elected institutions, constitutional courts and a binding referendum mechanism constrain the presidential government.
Focused six-question reassessment: Citizen signatures can initiate a binding referendum subject to substantive exclusions. Presidential terms and constitutional succession remain distinct from legislative discretion to freely replace a personally elected president.
axes.counterEvidence:
The May 2026 elected administration and security rhetoric are not assumed to have removed constitutional checks. Article 105/129 permits repeal referendums with excluded matters; head-of-government removal is checked separately from immunity suspension.
The owner-defined broader axis includes lawful delegation and direct public control; a lower numerical placement is not a regime classification. Six exact responses and response strengths remain inferred. Retained source access dates are not refreshed unless a source was actually revisited. Unchanged answers and other axes were not re-audited. Citizen signatures can initiate a binding referendum subject to substantive exclusions. Presidential terms and constitutional succession remain distinct from legislative discretion to freely replace a personally elected president.

answers.rationale: Educated assumption: Regular competitive presidential and legislative elections determine national leadership; the 2026 election and transition are verified. Most likely Strongly agree. The cited facts provide contextual evidence for an institutional estimate, not a verified explicit national endorsement of this exact statement. Formal constitutional provisions do not alone establish their practical independence or an explicit endorsement of the exact institutional rule.

Educated assumption: Agree is the most likely response to the revised claim “Important national policy decisions should be delegated to independent experts who do not need approval from elected representatives for each decision.” in the specified scope (Contemporary institutions and implemented policy; intended cut-off 2026-10-04). The retained sourced research records: Competitive elected institutions, constitutional courts and a binding referendum mechanism constrain the presidential government. Focused interpretation: Citizen signatures can initiate a binding referendum subject to substantive exclusions. Presidential terms and constitutional succession remain distinct from legislative discretion to freely replace a personally elected president. This is delegation of policy decisions to independent specialists, not replacement of the electorate or a claim that all expertise is political sovereignty. A legislative mandate, appointment process and later review can coexist with not voting on every operational decision.  The described institutional delegation or bounded permission makes agreement more likely than disagreement. Legal safeguards, narrower implementation or an inferred historical application make ordinary agreement more appropriate than an unconditional strong response. The citations supply contextual evidence, not a documented exact response to this new wording. The original source dossier is used as retained research; this pass does not claim a fresh retrieval or complete verification of every historical citation. Precise policy scope, hypothetical institutional translations and response intensity remain uncertain.

axes.brief: Operational CEN-CINAI services use stimulating environments, caregiving and learned social skills as causal developmental interventions.
axes.counterEvidence: These interventions do not quantitatively rank biology for every trait. Trait-specific educated assumptions disclose uncertainty and do not fabricate country-IQ, inherited racial violence or wage-value findings.
